70	class TokenRegistry:
71	    """In-process map of bearer tokens to an organization and a role.
72	
73	    Credentials live only for the lifetime of this instance: a restart
74	    starts with an empty registry and no protected entry point accepts any
75	    token. Registration is idempotent for an identical record; a token can
76	    never be rebound to a different organization or role. The same lock that
77	    guards the map also wraps the decide-and-commit sequence of a write
78	    request, so the authorization decision and the ledger/inventory mutation
79	    are indivisible.
80	    """
81	
82	    def __init__(self) -> None:
83	        self._tokens: dict[str, Subject] = {}
84	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
85	
86	    def register(
87	        self, token: str, organization_id: str, role: str
88	    ) -> tuple[str, Subject]:
89	        """Register a token or reconcile an identical resubmission.
90	
91	        Returns ``("created", subject)`` for a new token, ``("exists",
92	        subject)`` for a resubmission carrying the same organization and
93	        role, or ``("conflict", existing)`` when the token is already bound
94	        to different credentials. Only ``"created"`` adds a record.
95	        """
96	        with self._lock:
97	            existing = self._tokens.get(token)
98	            if existing is None:
99	                subject = Subject(organization_id, role)
100	                self._tokens[token] = subject
101	                return "created", subject
102	            if existing.organization_id == organization_id and existing.role == role:
103	                return "exists", existing
104	            return "conflict", existing
105	
106	    def lookup(self, token: str) -> Subject | None:
107	        with self._lock:
108	            return self._tokens.get(token)
109	
110	    def run_locked(self, commit: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
111	        """Run ``commit`` holding the registry lock.
112	
113	        Snapshot and branch creation make their single role decision earlier
114	        (from the request-scoped subject) and then run the capture/fork
115	        sequence here, so it stays indivisible from every other
116	        registry-guarded write without re-reading a credential.
117	        """
118	        with self._lock:
119	            return commit()
120	
121	    def commit_write(
122	        self,
123	        token: str,
124	        organization_id: str,
125	        commit: Callable[[], Any],
126	    ) -> tuple[str, Any]:
127	        """Authorize a write and run ``commit`` under one lock.
128	
129	        The token is re-checked against the registry, its organization must
130	        match the request's organization, and its role must be ``write``;
131	        only then does ``commit`` run, still holding the registry lock. The
132	        status is ``"ok"`` with the commit result or ``"forbidden"`` (the
133	        commit is never invoked). Reaching the store this way makes a
134	        rejected request incapable of changing the ledger or inventory.
135	        """
136	        with self._lock:
137	            subject = self._tokens.get(token)
138	            if (
139	                subject is None
140	                or subject.organization_id != organization_id
141	                or subject.role != "write"
142	            ):
143	                return "forbidden", None
144	            return "ok", commit()

311	class ReservationInventory:
312	    """In-process reservation ledger with per-resource capacity control.
313	
314	    Resource capacities are fixed by the first reservation that names the
315	    resource and are never rewritten. The balance check and the deduction
316	    happen inside a single lock, so concurrent requests can neither oversell
317	    a resource nor lose each other's writes. State lives only for the
318	    lifetime of this instance.
319	    """
320	
321	    def __init__(self) -> None:
322	        self._capacities: dict[str, int] = {}
323	        self._reservations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
324	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
325	
326	    def _occupied_locked(self, resource_id: str) -> int:
327	        return sum(
328	            record["quantity"]
329	            for record in self._reservations.values()
330	            if record["resourceId"] == resource_id
331	        )
332	
333	    def _view_locked(self, record: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
334	        capacity = self._capacities[record["resourceId"]]
335	        occupied = self._occupied_locked(record["resourceId"])
336	        return {
337	            "organizationId": record["organizationId"],
338	            "reservationId": record["reservationId"],
339	            "resourceId": record["resourceId"],
340	            "quantity": record["quantity"],
341	            "capacity": capacity,
342	            "occupied": occupied,
343	            "remaining": capacity - occupied,
344	        }
345	
346	    def reserve(
347	        self, reservation: dict[str, Any]
348	    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
349	        """Commit a reservation or reconcile a replay, atomically.
350	
351	        Returns ``(status, view)`` where status is ``"created"`` for a new
352	        reservationId, ``"exists"`` for an identical replay (nothing is
353	        counted twice), ``"reservation_conflict"`` when the reservationId
354	        exists with different fields, ``"capacity_conflict"`` when the
355	        resource's recorded capacity differs from the declared one, or
356	        ``"capacity_exceeded"`` when the remaining balance cannot cover the
357	        quantity. Only ``"created"`` mutates state; the view carries the
358	        post-commit occupied and remaining balances.
359	        """
360	        with self._lock:
361	            existing = self._reservations.get(reservation["reservationId"])
362	            if existing is not None:
363	                if all(
364	                    existing[field] == reservation[field]
365	                    for field in RESERVATION_FIELDS
366	                ):
367	                    return "exists", self._view_locked(existing)
368	                return "reservation_conflict", None
369	
370	            resource_id = reservation["resourceId"]
371	            recorded = self._capacities.get(resource_id)
372	            if recorded is not None and recorded != reservation["capacity"]:
373	                return "capacity_conflict", None
374	            capacity = recorded if recorded is not None else reservation["capacity"]
375	
376	            occupied = self._occupied_locked(resource_id)
377	            if reservation["quantity"] > capacity - occupied:
378	                return "capacity_exceeded", None
379	
380	            stored = {field: reservation[field] for field in RESERVATION_FIELDS}
381	            self._capacities[resource_id] = capacity
382	            self._reservations[stored["reservationId"]] = stored
383	            return "created", self._view_locked(stored)
384	
385	    def list_for_organization(self, organization_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
386	        with self._lock:
387	            views = [
388	                self._view_locked(record)
389	                for record in self._reservations.values()
390	                if record["organizationId"] == organization_id
391	            ]
392	        views.sort(key=lambda view: (view["resourceId"], view["reservationId"]))
393	        return views
394	
395	    def capacity_count(self) -> int:
396	        with self._lock:
397	            return len(self._capacities)
398	
399	    def reservation_count(self) -> int:
400	        with self._lock:
401	            return len(self._reservations)
402	
403	    def snapshot(self) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
404	        """Return deep, locked copies of capacities and reservations."""
405	        with self._lock:
406	            capacities = dict(self._capacities)
407	            reservations = {
408	                reservation_id: dict(record)
409	                for reservation_id, record in self._reservations.items()
410	            }
411	        return capacities, reservations

413	    def snapshot_for_organization(
414	        self, organization_id: str
415	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, int], dict[str, dict[str, Any]]]:
416	        """Locked copies of capacities/reservations visible to one org.
417	
418	        Capacities are included only for resources the organization itself
419	        reserves; reservations of other organizations are never captured.
420	        """
421	        with self._lock:
422	            reservations = {

424	                for reservation_id, record in self._reservations.items()

427	            capacities = {

430	                if resource_id in {r["resourceId"] for r in reservations.values()}

432	        return capacities, reservations

437	        reservations: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
438	    ) -> None:
439	        """Replace capacities and reservations with deep copies."""

443	                reservation_id: dict(record)

1005	def evaluate_decision(occurred: list[int], params: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
1006	    """Compute the peak window and resulting action from matching timestamps.
1007

1009	    and type). Window boundaries are left-closed/right-open and start at
1010	    zero. Ties on the peak count resolve to the earliest window start.
1011	    """
1012	    window_size = params["windowSize"]
1013	    threshold = params["threshold"]
1014	    from_value = params["from"]
1015	    to_value = params["to"]
1016	
1017	    counts: dict[int, int] = {}
1018	    for timestamp in occurred:
1019	        if from_value is not None and not (from_value <= timestamp <= to_value):
1020	            continue
1021	        start = (timestamp // window_size) * window_size
1022	        counts[start] = counts.get(start, 0) + 1
1023	
1024	    if from_value is None:
1025	        # Only windows actually covered by matching events.
1026	        starts = sorted(counts)
1027	    else:
1028	        # Every window intersecting the closed interval [from, to], kept
1029	        # (including empty ones) so the audit can reconcile the result.
1030	        first = (from_value // window_size) * window_size
1031	        last = (to_value // window_size) * window_size
1032	        starts = list(range(first, last + 1, window_size))

1036	    for start in starts:
1037	        count = counts.get(start, 0)

1040	            peak_start = start
1041	
1042	    action = "escalate" if peak_count >= threshold else "observe"
1043	    return {
1044	        "organizationId": params["organizationId"],
1045	        "type": params["type"],
1046	        "windowSize": window_size,
1047	        "from": from_value,
1048	        "to": to_value,
1049	        "peakStart": peak_start,

1425	def plan_allocation(params: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
1426	    """Allocate whole demands to resources by deterministic rules.
1427	
1428	    Demands are handled by priority descending, then demandId in Unicode
1429	    code-point order. A demand goes wholly to the lexicographically smallest
1430	    resourceId with enough remaining capacity; otherwise it is unassigned.
1431	    """
1432	    demands = params["demands"]
1433	    remaining = dict(params["resources"])
1434	
1435	    ordered_demands = sorted(
1436	        demands, key=lambda demand: (-demand["priority"], demand["demandId"])
1437	    )
1438	    ordered_resources = sorted(remaining)
1439	
1440	    assignments: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
1441	    unassigned: list[str] = []
1442	    total_units = 0
1443	    for demand in ordered_demands:
1444	        demand_id = demand["demandId"]
1445	        units = demand["units"]
1446	        chosen = None
1447	        for resource_id in ordered_resources:
1448	            if remaining[resource_id] >= units:
1449	                chosen = resource_id
1450	                break
1451	        if chosen is None:
1452	            unassigned.append(demand_id)
1453	            continue
1454	        remaining[chosen] -= units
1455	        assignments.append(
1456	            {"demandId": demand_id, "resourceId": chosen, "units": units}
1457	        )
1458	        total_units += units
1459	
1460	    unassigned.sort()
1461	    return {
1462	        "organizationId": params["organizationId"],
1463	        "assignments": assignments,
1464	        "unassigned": unassigned,
1465	        "totalUnits": total_units,
1466	    }

1469	def _windows_from_occurred(
1470	    occurred: list[int],
1471	    window_size: int,
1472	    from_value: int | None,
1473	    to_value: int | None,
1474	) -> list[dict[str, int]]:
1475	    """Build aggregate windows from a sorted timestamp snapshot.
1476	
1477	    Windows start at zero and cover ``[start, start + windowSize)``. Without
1478	    a range only windows actually hit by events are returned; with a range
1479	    every window intersecting the closed interval ``[from, to]`` is kept,
1480	    empty ones included. Windows are ordered by start ascending.
1481	    """
1482	    counts: dict[int, int] = {}
1483	    for timestamp in occurred:
1484	        if from_value is not None and not (from_value <= timestamp <= to_value):
1485	            continue
1486	        start = (timestamp // window_size) * window_size
1487	        counts[start] = counts.get(start, 0) + 1
1488	
1489	    if from_value is None:
1490	        # Only windows actually covered by matching events.
1491	        starts = sorted(counts)
1492	    else:
1493	        # Every window intersecting the closed interval [from, to].
1494	        first = (from_value // window_size) * window_size
1495	        last = (to_value // window_size) * window_size
1496	        starts = list(range(first, last + 1, window_size))
1497	
1498	    return [
1499	        {"start": start, "end": start + window_size, "count": counts.get(start, 0)}
1500	        for start in starts
1501	    ]

1506	) -> dict[int, int]:
1507	    """Count one side's matching events per window start, with range filter.
1508	
1509	    Shares the window division and closed-interval filtering used by the
1510	    aggregate and decision entry points.
1511	    """
1512	    window_size = params["windowSize"]
1513	    from_value = params["from"]
1514	    to_value = params["to"]
1515	    counts: dict[int, int] = {}
1516	    for timestamp in occurred:
1517	        if from_value is not None and not (from_value <= timestamp <= to_value):
1518	            continue
1519	        start = (timestamp // window_size) * window_size
1520	        counts[start] = counts.get(start, 0) + 1
1521	    return counts

1524	def _branch_window_starts(params: dict[str, Any]) -> list[int]:
1525	    """Window starts a comparison must align, using the aggregate contract.
1526	
1527	    Without a range there is no fixed grid; the caller unions the two sides'
1528	    hit windows. With a range every window intersecting the closed interval
1529	    is present, so both sides share the same start list.
1530	    """
1531	    if params["from"] is None:
1532	        return []
1533	    window_size = params["windowSize"]
1534	    first = (params["from"] // window_size) * window_size
1535	    last = (params["to"] // window_size) * window_size
1536	    return list(range(first, last + 1, window_size))

1539	def compare_branches(
1540	    left_occurred: list[int],
1541	    right_occurred: list[int],
1542	    params: dict[str, Any],
1543	) -> dict[str, Any]:
1544	    """Diff two branches' window counts and peaks from timestamp snapshots.
1545	
1546	    Each ``occurred`` list is a single locked snapshot of one branch's
1547	    matching events, so the window rows and the peak for a side derive from
1548	    the same read; nothing is written. Without a range, rows cover the union
1549	    of the two sides' hit windows; with a range, rows cover every window
1550	    intersecting ``[from, to]``, empty windows kept. Rows align by start
1551	    ascending and carry each side's count plus an ``equal`` marker. The
1552	    ``decision`` block holds each side's peak and action and a marker saying
1553	    whether the two peak results agree.
1554	    """
1555	    left_counts = _branch_window_counts(left_occurred, params)
1556	    right_counts = _branch_window_counts(right_occurred, params)
1557	
1558	    range_starts = _branch_window_starts(params)
1559	    if range_starts:
1560	        starts = range_starts
1561	    else:
1562	        starts = sorted(set(left_counts) | set(right_counts))
1563	
1564	    windows = []
1565	    for start in starts:
1566	        left_count = left_counts.get(start, 0)
1567	        right_count = right_counts.get(start, 0)
1568	        windows.append(
1569	            {
1570	                "start": start,
1571	                "leftCount": left_count,
1572	                "rightCount": right_count,
1573	                "equal": left_count == right_count,
1574	            }
1575	        )
1576	
1577	    left_peak = evaluate_decision(left_occurred, params)
1578	    right_peak = evaluate_decision(right_occurred, params)
1579	    left_decision = {
1580	        "peakStart": left_peak["peakStart"],
1581	        "peakCount": left_peak["peakCount"],
1582	        "action": left_peak["action"],
1583	    }
1584	    right_decision = {
1585	        "peakStart": right_peak["peakStart"],
1586	        "peakCount": right_peak["peakCount"],
1587	        "action": right_peak["action"],
1588	    }
1589	    decision = {
1590	        "left": left_decision,
1591	        "right": right_decision,
1592	        "equal": left_decision == right_decision,
1593	    }
1594	
1595	    return {
1596	        "organizationId": params["organizationId"],
1597	        "left": params["left"],
1598	        "right": params["right"],
1599	        "type": params["type"],
1600	        "windowSize": params["windowSize"],
1601	        "threshold": params["threshold"],
1602	        "from": params["from"],
1603	        "to": params["to"],
1604	        "decision": decision,
1605	        "windows": windows,
1606	    }

"""Shared test support for request-scoped credentials.

The service now authenticates every protected entry point with a Bearer
token bound to one organization. The pre-existing tests exercise many
organizations (org-1, org-2, org-a, unknown orgs, even verbatim whitespace
ids), so the low-level request helpers pick the credential organization from
each request itself and lazily register a write token for that exact
organization. Registration is cached per test/server instance.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import urllib.request
from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import parse_qs, urlsplit

DEFAULT_ORG = "org-1"


def select_organization(path: str, body: bytes | None) -> str | None:
    """Return the exact organization a request acts on, if determinable.

    A single, non-blank ``organizationId`` query parameter wins; otherwise a
    non-blank ``organizationId`` string in a JSON object body is used. The
    value is returned verbatim (whitespace kept) so the credential matches the
    service's exact comparison. Blank, duplicated, or absent ids return
    ``None``; those requests fail parameter/body validation (422) before the
    organization is ever compared.
    """
    query = urlsplit(path).query
    values = parse_qs(query, keep_blank_values=True).get("organizationId")
    if values and len(values) == 1 and values[0].strip():
        return values[0]

    if body is not None:
        try:
            data: Any = json.loads(body.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
            data = None
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            organization_id = data.get("organizationId")
            if isinstance(organization_id, str) and organization_id.strip():
                return organization_id
    return None


def ensure_token(cache: dict[str, str], base_url: str, organization_id: str) -> str:
    """Register (once) and return a write token for ``organization_id``."""
    token = cache.get(organization_id)
    if token is None:
        token = f"test-token-{len(cache) + 1}"
        payload = json.dumps(
            {
                "token": token,
                "organizationId": organization_id,
                "role": "write",
            }
        ).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request(
            f"{base_url}/auth/tokens",
            data=payload,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
            method="POST",
        )
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
            # 201 (new) or 200 (identical resubmission) are both fine.
            assert response.status in (200, 201)
        cache[organization_id] = token
    return token


def authorization_header(
    cache: dict[str, str], base_url: str, path: str, body: bytes | None
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Build the Authorization header for one outgoing test request."""
    organization_id = select_organization(path, body) or DEFAULT_ORG
    token = ensure_token(cache, base_url, organization_id)
    return {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"}

1	"""Regression tests for POST /branches/compare.

8	  window division and the decision peak/action rules;
9	- without a range the rows are the union of hit windows, aligned by start;
10	  with a range every intersecting window gets a row, empty ones kept;
11	- both-branches-empty yields ``windows: []`` and identical submissions are
12	  byte-for-byte stable;
13	- 401 / 403 / 404 (branch_not_found) / 422 / 415 / 400 follow the fixed
14	  ordering, left is always resolved before right, and nothing is ever
15	  written or implicitly created, including across organizations.

"""Regression tests for POST /branches/compare.

The branch simulator already ran each branch in isolation; this locks down
the new read-only entry point that compares two branches' window counts and
peak decisions:

- each side is recomputed from that branch's own events with the aggregate
  window division and the decision peak/action rules;
- without a range the rows are the union of hit windows, aligned by start;
  with a range every intersecting window gets a row, empty ones kept;
- both-branches-empty yields ``windows: []`` and identical submissions are
  byte-for-byte stable;
- 401 / 403 / 404 (branch_not_found) / 422 / 415 / 400 follow the fixed
  ordering, left is always resolved before right, and nothing is ever
  written or implicitly created, including across organizations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import unittest
from typing import Any
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

from event_sim.server import create_server

ORG1 = "org-1"
ORG2 = "org-2"
EVENT_TYPE = "incident.created"


def event_body(event_id: str, occurred_at: int, organization_id: str = ORG1) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "eventId": event_id,
        "organizationId": organization_id,
        "type": EVENT_TYPE,
        "occurredAt": occurred_at,
        "payload": {},
    }


class BranchCompareTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.server = create_server(port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"
        self.register("w1", ORG1, "write")
        self.register("w2", ORG2, "write")
        self.register("r1", ORG1, "read")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=2)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- low level

    def raw(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        body: bytes | None = None,
        token: str | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
        headers: dict[str, str] = {}
        if content_type is not None:
            headers["Content-Type"] = content_type
        if token is not None:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        request = Request(
            f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=body, headers=headers, method=method
        )
        try:
            with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
                return response.status, response.read()
        except HTTPError as error:
            try:
                return error.code, error.read()
            finally:
                error.close()

    def call(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        payload: Any = None,
        token: str | None = "w1",
        raw_body: bytes | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        body = (
            raw_body
            if raw_body is not None
            else json.dumps(payload).encode() if payload is not None
            else None
        )
        status, raw = self.raw(
            path,
            method=method,
            body=body,
            token=token,
            content_type=content_type,
        )
        return status, json.loads(raw)

                "organizationId": organization_id,

def validate_branch_event_compare_request(data: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Validate a decoded JSON body for POST /branches/compare/events.

    Exactly ``organizationId``, ``left`` and ``right`` — all non-empty
    strings. ``left`` and ``right`` are branch names; the same name on both
    sides is legal.

    keys = set(data)
    expected = set(BRANCH_EVENT_COMPARE_FIELDS)
    if keys != expected:
        missing = sorted(expected - keys)
        unknown = sorted(keys - expected)
        detail = []
        if missing:
            detail.append(f"missing fields: {', '.join(missing)}")
        if unknown:
            detail.append(f"unexpected fields: {', '.join(unknown)}")
        raise EventValidationError("; ".join(detail))
    for field in BRANCH_EVENT_COMPARE_FIELDS:
        value = data[field]

    return {field: data[field] for field in BRANCH_EVENT_COMPARE_FIELDS}

### `POST /branches/compare/events`

A read-only, event-level comparison of two existing branches. Where
`POST /branches/compare` aligns window counts, this entry point aligns the
two branches' events by `eventId` and reports the deterministic difference
summary. Nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or in the main
service is read for mutation or written, and identical submissions return
byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call
it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound
to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object
containing exactly these fields:

| Field            | Rule                                                          |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |

Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
are then equal by construction and every shared event lands in `same`.

Events are aligned by `eventId`:

- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left branch.
- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right branch.
- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose events are identical in every
  field except `eventId`; payloads compare by content, so key order inside
  a payload never matters.
- `diff` — identifiers on both sides whose events disagree. Each entry is
  `{"eventId", "fields"}`, where `fields` names the mismatched fields
  (drawn from `organizationId`, `type`, `occurredAt`, `payload`).

Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
neither branch holds any event, all four groups are empty arrays and all
four counts are `0`.

The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:

```json
{"diff":[{"eventId":"evt-2","fields":["occurredAt","payload"]}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["evt-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["evt-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["evt-3"],"sameCount":1}
```

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare/events \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b"}'
```

- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
  registered.
- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.

Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.

"""Regression tests for POST /branches/compare/events.

The window-level branch comparison already existed; this locks down the new
read-only entry point that aligns two branches' events by eventId:

- identifiers only on one side land in leftOnly/rightOnly, identical shared
  events in same (payloads compare by content), and disagreeing shared
  events in diff with the mismatched field names;
- each group is code-point sorted and paired with a ``<group>Count`` key,
  and the response is compact, key-sorted JSON with one trailing newline;
- both-branches-empty yields four empty groups and zero counts, and
  identical submissions are byte-for-byte stable;
- 401 / 403 / 404 (branch_not_found) / 422 / 415 / 400 follow the fixed
  ordering, left is always resolved before right, and nothing is ever
  written or implicitly created, including across organizations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import unittest
from typing import Any
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

from event_sim.server import create_server

ORG1 = "org-1"
ORG2 = "org-2"
EVENT_TYPE = "incident.created"


def event_body(
    event_id: str,
    occurred_at: int,
    organization_id: str = ORG1,
    payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    event_type: str = EVENT_TYPE,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "eventId": event_id,
        "organizationId": organization_id,
        "type": event_type,
        "occurredAt": occurred_at,
        "payload": {} if payload is None else payload,
    }


class BranchEventCompareTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.server = create_server(port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"
        self.register("w1", ORG1, "write")
        self.register("w2", ORG2, "write")
        self.register("r1", ORG1, "read")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=2)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- low level

    def raw(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        body: bytes | None = None,
        token: str | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
        headers: dict[str, str] = {}
        if content_type is not None:
            headers["Content-Type"] = content_type
        if token is not None:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        request = Request(
            f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=body, headers=headers, method=method
        )
        try:
            with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
                return response.status, response.read()
        except HTTPError as error:
            try:
                return error.code, error.read()
            finally:
                error.close()

    def call(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        payload: Any = None,
        token: str | None = "w1",
        raw_body: bytes | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        body = (
            raw_body
            if raw_body is not None
            else json.dumps(payload).encode() if payload is not None
            else None
        )
        status, raw = self.raw(
            path,
            method=method,
            body=body,
            token=token,
            content_type=content_type,
        )
        return status, json.loads(raw)

    def register(self, token: str, organization_id: str, role: str) -> None:
        status, _ = self.call(
            "/auth/tokens",
            method="POST",
            token=None,
            payload={
                "token": token,
                "organizationId": organization_id,
                "role": role,
            },
        )
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 201))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- scaffolding

    def fork_branches(
        self,
        *,
        snapshot_id: str = "s1",
        branches: tuple[str, ...] = ("left", "right"),
        token: str = "w1",
    ) -> None:
        status, _ = self.call(
            "/snapshots",
            method="POST",
            token=token,
            payload={"snapshotId": snapshot_id},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)
        for branch_id in branches:
            status, _ = self.call(
                "/branches",
                method="POST",
                token=token,
                payload={"branchId": branch_id, "snapshotId": snapshot_id},
            )
            self.assertEqual(status, 201)

    def add_branch_event(
        self,
        branch: str,
        event_id: str,
        occurred_at: int,
        token: str = "w1",
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        organization_id = ORG1 if token == "w1" else ORG2
        status, _ = self.call(
            f"/branches/{branch}/events",
            method="POST",
            token=token,
            payload=event_body(event_id, occurred_at, organization_id, **kwargs),
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)

    def compare_payload(self, **overrides: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
        payload: dict[str, Any] = {
            "organizationId": ORG1,
            "left": "left",
            "right": "right",
        }
        payload.update(overrides)
        return payload

    def compare(
        self, payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None, *, token: str | None = "w1"
    ) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        return self.call(
            "/branches/compare/events",
            method="POST",
            payload=self.compare_payload() if payload is None else payload,
            token=token,
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- happy paths

    def test_events_align_by_identifier_into_four_groups(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        # Shared and identical.
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-same", 10, payload={"severity": "low"})
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-same", 10, payload={"severity": "low"})
        # Shared but occurredAt and payload differ.
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-diff", 20, payload={"severity": "low"})
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-diff", 25, payload={"severity": "high"})
        # Shared but only the type differs.
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-typed", 30)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-typed", 30, event_type="incident.updated")
        # One side each.
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-left", 40)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-right", 50)

        status, body = self.compare()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnly"], ["evt-left"])
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnlyCount"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(body["rightOnly"], ["evt-right"])
        self.assertEqual(body["rightOnlyCount"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(body["same"], ["evt-same"])
        self.assertEqual(body["sameCount"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(
            body["diff"],
            [
                {"eventId": "evt-diff", "fields": ["occurredAt", "payload"]},
                {"eventId": "evt-typed", "fields": ["type"]},
            ],
        )
        self.assertEqual(body["diffCount"], 2)

    def test_payload_compares_by_content_not_key_order(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event(
            "left", "evt-1", 10, payload={"a": 1, "b": {"x": 1, "y": 2}}
        )
        # Same content, different key order at both levels.
        status, _ = self.call(
            "/branches/right/events",
            method="POST",
            token="w1",
            payload={
                "eventId": "evt-1",
                "organizationId": ORG1,
                "type": EVENT_TYPE,
                "occurredAt": 10,
                "payload": {"b": {"y": 2, "x": 1}, "a": 1},
            },
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 201)

        status, body = self.compare()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["same"], ["evt-1"])
        self.assertEqual(body["diff"], [])

    def test_identifiers_sort_in_code_point_order(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        for event_id in ("evt-b", "evt-A", "evt-a", "evt-1"):
            self.add_branch_event("left", event_id, 10)
        status, body = self.compare()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnly"], ["evt-1", "evt-A", "evt-a", "evt-b"])
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnlyCount"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(body["rightOnly"], [])

    def test_same_branch_on_both_sides_is_legal_and_fully_same(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches(branches=("left",))
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-2", 20, payload={"k": "v"})
        payload = self.compare_payload(right="left")
        status, body = self.compare(payload)
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["same"], ["evt-1", "evt-2"])
        self.assertEqual(body["sameCount"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnly"], [])
        self.assertEqual(body["rightOnly"], [])
        self.assertEqual(body["diff"], [])
        self.assertEqual(body["diffCount"], 0)

    def test_empty_branches_yield_empty_groups_and_zero_counts(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        status, body = self.compare()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {
                "leftOnly": [],
                "leftOnlyCount": 0,
                "rightOnly": [],
                "rightOnlyCount": 0,
                "same": [],
                "sameCount": 0,
                "diff": [],
                "diffCount": 0,
            },
        )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------- byte contract

    def test_response_is_compact_sorted_integer_and_newline_terminated(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)

        raw_body = json.dumps(self.compare_payload()).encode()
        status, raw = self.raw(
            "/branches/compare/events", method="POST", body=raw_body, token="w1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(raw[-1:], b"\n")
        self.assertEqual(raw.count(b"\n"), 1)
        self.assertNotIn(b", ", raw)
        self.assertNotIn(b": ", raw)
        # Counts stay integers.
        self.assertIn(b'"leftOnlyCount":1', raw)
        self.assertIn(b'"diffCount":0', raw)
        # Keys are sorted by code point at every level.
        body = json.loads(raw)
        self.assertEqual(
            list(body),
            [
                "diff",
                "diffCount",
                "leftOnly",
                "leftOnlyCount",
                "rightOnly",
                "rightOnlyCount",
                "same",
                "sameCount",
            ],
        )

    def test_diff_entry_keys_are_sorted(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-1", 20)
        raw_body = json.dumps(self.compare_payload()).encode()
        status, raw = self.raw(
            "/branches/compare/events", method="POST", body=raw_body, token="w1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        body = json.loads(raw)
        self.assertEqual(list(body["diff"][0]), ["eventId", "fields"])

    def test_repeated_submissions_are_byte_identical(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-2", 20)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-2", 25)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-3", 30)
        raw_body = json.dumps(self.compare_payload()).encode()
        raws = [
            self.raw(
                "/branches/compare/events", method="POST", body=raw_body, token="w1"
            )[1]
            for _ in range(3)
        ]
        self.assertEqual(len(set(raws)), 1)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- read-only

    def test_compare_is_read_only(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-2", 20)

        def summaries() -> tuple[Any, Any]:
            left = self.call("/branches/left")[1]
            right = self.call("/branches/right")[1]
            return left, right

        before = summaries()
        for _ in range(3):
            status, _ = self.compare()
            self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        after = summaries()
        self.assertEqual(before, after)

        # Main-service state and alerts are untouched as well.
        status, events = self.call("/events?organizationId=org-1")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(events["events"], [])
        status, alerts = self.call("/alerts?organizationId=org-1")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(alerts["alerts"], [])

    def test_failed_compare_creates_no_branch(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        for payload in (
            self.compare_payload(left="ghost"),
            self.compare_payload(right="ghost"),
            self.compare_payload(left=""),
        ):
            status, _ = self.compare(payload)
            self.assertIn(status, (404, 422))
        self.assertEqual(self.call("/branches/ghost")[0], 404)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ roles / auth

    def test_read_credential_may_compare(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-1", 10)
        status, body = self.compare(token="r1")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["leftOnly"], ["evt-1"])

    def test_missing_or_unregistered_credential_is_401(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        raw_body = json.dumps(self.compare_payload()).encode()
        status, body = self.raw(
            "/branches/compare/events", method="POST", body=raw_body, token=None
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["error"], "unauthorized")
        status, body = self.raw(
            "/branches/compare/events",
            method="POST",
            body=raw_body,
            token="forged",
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(body)["error"], "unauthorized")

    # -------------------------------------------------------- organization 403

    def test_foreign_organization_request_is_403_before_branch_lookup(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.fork_branches(snapshot_id="s2", branches=("foreign",), token="w2")

        # An ORG2 credential naming ORG1 is rejected on the organization
        # decision even when the branch names do not exist anywhere.
        status, body = self.compare(
            self.compare_payload(left="nope", right="also-nope"), token="w2"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "forbidden")

        # An ORG1 credential naming ORG2's branch cannot read it.
        status, body = self.compare(
            self.compare_payload(left="foreign", right="left"), token="w1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "forbidden")
        status, body = self.compare(
            self.compare_payload(left="left", right="foreign"), token="w1"
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 403)
        self.assertEqual(body["error"], "forbidden")

    def test_branch_existence_checked_left_then_right(self) -> None:
        self.fork_branches()
        self.fork_branches(snapshot_id="s2", branches=("foreign",), token="w2")

        # Unknown names are 404 branch_not_found; no branch is created.
        status, body = self.compare(self.compare_payload(left="ghost"))
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)

"""Regression tests for POST /branches/compare/events.

The window-level branch comparison already existed; this locks down the new
read-only entry point that aligns two branches' events by eventId:

- identifiers only on one side land in leftOnly/rightOnly, identical shared
  events in same (payloads compare by content), and disagreeing shared
  events in diff with the mismatched field names;
- each group is code-point sorted and paired with a ``<group>Count`` key,
  and the response is compact, key-sorted JSON with one trailing newline;
- both-branches-empty yields four empty groups and zero counts, and
  identical submissions are byte-for-byte stable;
- 401 / 403 / 404 (branch_not_found) / 422 / 415 / 400 follow the fixed
  ordering, left is always resolved before right, and nothing is ever
  written or implicitly created, including across organizations.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
import unittest
from typing import Any
from urllib.error import HTTPError
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen

from event_sim.server import create_server

ORG1 = "org-1"
ORG2 = "org-2"
EVENT_TYPE = "incident.created"


def event_body(
    event_id: str,
    occurred_at: int,
    organization_id: str = ORG1,
    payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    event_type: str = EVENT_TYPE,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "eventId": event_id,
        "organizationId": organization_id,
        "type": event_type,
        "occurredAt": occurred_at,
        "payload": {} if payload is None else payload,
    }


class BranchEventCompareTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self.server = create_server(port=0)
        self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.thread.start()
        self.base_url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_port}"
        self.register("w1", ORG1, "write")
        self.register("w2", ORG2, "write")
        self.register("r1", ORG1, "read")

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()
        self.thread.join(timeout=2)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------- low level

    def raw(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        body: bytes | None = None,
        token: str | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, bytes]:
        headers: dict[str, str] = {}
        if content_type is not None:
            headers["Content-Type"] = content_type
        if token is not None:
            headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {token}"
        request = Request(
            f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=body, headers=headers, method=method
        )
        try:
            with urlopen(request, timeout=5) as response:
                return response.status, response.read()
        except HTTPError as error:
            try:
                return error.code, error.read()
            finally:
                error.close()

    def call(
        self,
        path: str,
        *,
        method: str = "GET",
        payload: Any = None,
        token: str | None = "w1",
        raw_body: bytes | None = None,
        content_type: str | None = "application/json",
    ) -> tuple[int, Any]:
        body = (
            raw_body
            if raw_body is not None
            else json.dumps(payload).encode() if payload is not None
            else None
        )
        status, raw = self.raw(
            path,
            method=method,
            body=body,
            token=token,
            content_type=content_type,
        )
        return status, json.loads(raw)

    def register(self, token: str, organization_id: str, role: str) -> None:
        status, _ = self.call(
            "/auth/tokens",
            method="POST",
            token=None,
            payload={
                "token": token,
                "organizationId": organization_id,
                "role": role,
            },
        )
        self.assertIn(status, (200, 201))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------- scaffolding

    def fork_branches(
        self,
        *,
        snapshot_id: str = "s1",
        branches: tuple[str, ...] = ("left", "right"),
        token: str = "w1",
    ) -> None:
        status, _ = self.call(
            "/snapshots",
            method="POST",
            token=token,
            payload={"snapshotId": snapshot_id},

        for branch_id in branches:

    def add_branch_event(
        self,

            f"/branches/{branch}/events",

        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-diff", 25, payload={"severity": "high"})

        self.add_branch_event("left", "evt-typed", 30)
        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-typed", 30, event_type="incident.updated")
        # One side each.

        self.add_branch_event("right", "evt-right", 50)

        status, body = self.compare()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)

        self.assertEqual(body["rightOnly"], ["evt-right"])

        self.assertEqual(
